title: Localization at one
statement:
After the canonical identifications $A_1\cong A$, the Rees localization
equivalence at $1$ is the identity.

proof.text:
Both the localization equivalence and the identity send each homogeneous
monomial $at^n$ to itself under $A_1\cong A$. Use
[lemma-nagata-rees-sum-components] and ring-homomorphism extensionality.

blueprint_notes.label: status
blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its
charts are the construction `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineBlowup`, with
`AffineBlowup.chart` and
`AffineBlowup.isLocalization_away_map` supplying the chart algebra
and its localization coherence, so neither is rebuilt by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
After the canonical identification $A_1\cong A$, the Rees localization map
at $1$ is the identity: the composite of
$\rho_1\colon\mathcal R_A(I)\to\mathcal R_{A_1}(IA_1)$ with the
coefficientwise map induced by $A_1\cong A$ is the identity of
$\mathcal R_A(I)$. Consequently the same holds for the induced morphisms of
affine blow-ups.

proof.text:
Coefficientwise maps compose like the underlying ring homomorphisms, and
the composite $A\to A_1\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ is the identity. Hence the
composite of the two coefficientwise maps sends each homogeneous monomial
$at^n$ to itself, so it is the identity by
[lemma-nagata-rees-sum-components] and ring-homomorphism extensionality.
The morphisms of affine blow-ups are induced on Proj compatibly with
composition and identities, which gives the second statement.
